note: Authored teaching scenario. Every observation, prediction and record below was written for this exercise. None was produced by running image software or by examining an image, and nothing here supports a claim about how any real tool or forensic technique behaves.

tolerance.note: A scenario rule, not an empirically validated forensic tolerance. It is set for this exercise so you can apply a stated threshold consistently. A route is compatible on file size when its prediction is within 15 KB of the observed size. If more than one route satisfies that, file size does not distinguish them — which is a fact about this evidence, not a claim that the files are identical.

routes.label: Route A — resize once, save once
Route B — save, resize, save again
steps: Reopen that saved file and resize to 1200 x 800

sharedFinalStepNote: Both routes end with the same save, so the final encode settings cannot separate them. Any record that shows only the last operation is therefore uninformative here, however detailed it looks.

evidenceMenu.item: Retained transformation record for Output 7, with file hashes
evidenceMenu.result:
Transformation record, retained in full for this output

  input   interim-2400x1600.jpg   sha256 4c9f...a71e
  resize  2400x1600 -> 1200x800   filter=lanczos
  output  output-7-1200x800.jpg   sha256 0b32...9dd4

  Hash of the file named as input, taken from the working directory
  at the time of the operation: sha256 4c9f...a71e  (matches)

The record names what this operation read and what it wrote, and the
input hash matches a file that was present.
evidenceMenu.why: This record links Output 7 to a full-size JPEG: it names that file as the input to the resize, and the hash matches. Route A resizes the source directly and never has a full-size JPEG to read, so route A is excluded. It does not establish route B: any history that saved at full size before resizing would produce a record of this shape.

evidenceMenu.result:
Working directory listing, retained

  2027-03-02  09:14  source-2400x1600.tif      11,240 KB
  2027-03-02  09:41  interim-2400x1600.jpg      1,903 KB
  2027-03-02  09:52  output-7-1200x800.jpg          148 KB

A file-system listing. It records what existed and when. It does not
record what read what.
evidenceMenu.why: The listing shows that a full-size JPEG existed before the output, which looks decisive and is not. It does not show that Output 7 was made from that JPEG. The interim file could be an unrelated export, with Output 7 produced from the source directly. Co-existence is not descent, and asking for this listing is reasonable without settling anything.

evidenceMenu.item: Handover note retained with the output
evidenceMenu.result:
Note retained with the output, author's initials only

  "Resized for the newsletter — 1200 wide as requested. Big version
   is in the shared folder if anyone needs it. Didn't keep the
   in-between stuff."

  No date. No further pages retained.
evidenceMenu.why: A human record, and the only evidence here that was not generated by software. It confirms a resize and the existence of a full-size file somewhere, and it is silent about whether the big version was read to make the output or merely sat alongside it. That is the same gap as E2, arrived at from a different direction.

evidenceMenu.item: EXIF metadata dump for the output
evidenceMenu.unavailableBecause: No EXIF survives in the output, and no intermediate metadata was retained.
evidenceMenu.why: Listed because it is the first thing most people ask for. It is not available here, which is itself worth recording in your report.

evidenceMenu.item: Upload log from the service the output was distributed through
evidenceMenu.unavailableBecause: Not retained by the service, and the course has no account with it.
evidenceMenu.why: Would have been informative. It does not exist.

reveal.truth: Output 7 was produced by route B.
reveal.whyBothFit: Every field required to match exactly does match under both routes: dimensions, chroma subsampling and the absence of EXIF. On file size, route A's prediction is 6 KB from the observed 148 KB and route B's is 7 KB, both within the 15 KB scenario rule, so file size does not distinguish them. Both routes also end with the same save at quality 78, so the final encode settings cannot distinguish them either.
reveal.whatResolvesIt: E1, and only because it links rather than lists. The transformation record names a full-size JPEG as the input to the resize and the input hash matches a file that was present. Route A resizes the source directly and never has a full-size JPEG to read, so route A is excluded.
reveal.whatDoesNot: E2 and E3 both show that a full-size JPEG existed, and neither shows that Output 7 was made from it. The interim file could be an unrelated export. Co-existence is not descent. A student who chose either, noticed that gap and reported the question as still open has done the week correctly — and has arrived at the distinction the week is for.
reveal.limits: Excluding route A is not establishing route B. Every history that saved at full size before resizing would produce a record of E1's shape: a save at a different quality then a resize, or a route through a third intermediate size. Two routes were proposed, which is a fact about who was asked. The evidence supports the weaker claim, 'not route A, and consistent with route B'. Every record in this pack is authored, and none of it demonstrates the behaviour of real software.

distinguishingValuesNote: The settings that appear in one route and not the other. Route A has no unique setting — what distinguishes it is the absence of a save before the resize, and an absence cannot leak. Any record shown to a student as non-discriminating must contain none of these, or it separates the routes whatever its label says.
